title: Bi pride banner in cross-stitch
subtitle: The bisexual pride flag stripes as a horizontal banner on 14-count Aida
excerpt: A bi pride banner is a 90-by-50 stitch piece on 14-count Aida. The three bisexual pride flag stripes, pink (wider), lavender (narrow), and blue (wider), fill a simple rectangular banner shape outlined with a thin dark border. Three floss colours plus one border colour. Finished size is about 16 x 9 cm.
sourceNotes: Original design for Homemade cross-stitch library. The bisexual pride flag was designed by Michael Page in 1998.

. The three stripes of the bisexual pride flag, a wider pink band at the top, a narrow lavender band in the middle, and a wider blue band below, fill a rectangular shape. A thin

colours fill the stripes; a fourth is the border. Finished size is about 16 x 9 cm in a 15 cm hoop or a rectangular frame.

items.name: 14-count Aida, white or cream
items.substitutions: Pale cream gives the pink stripe a warmer tone

items.name: DMC floss
items.qty: 1 skein each: 3805 (bright pink), 210 (lavender), 796 (royal blue), 823 (navy for border)

items.name: Hoop or frame
items.qty: 15 cm (6 inch) hoop or small rectangular frame

content.text: Find the fabric centre. The chart centre falls in the lavender stripe. Begin with the lavender band (210), it is 8 stitches deep and the narrowest stripe, so placing it accurately first makes the wider stripes easier to align.
Work the pink band (20 stitches deep) above the lavender, then the blue band (20 stitches deep) below.
Add the navy back-stitch border around the outside of the rectangle after all the fill stitches are complete.
Wash gently and press face-down. A white mount and thin dark frame, or displayed as-is in the hoop, both work well.

items.symptom: The three stripes are not the same width
items.cause: The row count for the middle stripe was not checked against the chart before stitching.
items.fix: Count the chart rows for each stripe before threading. The bi flag uses pink (8 rows), lavender (2 rows), blue (8 rows) in the traditional ratio. Mark the row boundaries on the fabric with a thread tack before starting. Once the boundaries are set, stitch within them.

items.symptom: The lettering inside the banner sits too low
items.cause: The text was placed relative to the base of the fabric rather than the centre of the banner area.
items.fix: Find the horizontal centre of the banner and position the text midline from there. Once the centre row is marked, count up half the letter height and begin the top of the first letter from that point.

content.text: The coming-out hoop in this sub-category adds a text element to a flag piece. Try it once a plain banner feels comfortable.

glossaryTerms.definition: A stiff, evenly-woven cross-stitch fabric with clearly visible squares formed by groups of threads. The default for beginners. Counted in squares per inch: 11ct, 14ct, 16ct, and 18ct are the common counts.

A solid outline stitch worked in a single strand along the back-stitch layer of the chart. You stitch backwards along the line one stitch at a time, each stitch finishing where the previous one started.

The six-strand embroidery thread used for cross-stitch. Each skein is made of six strands twisted together loosely; the stitcher strips out the number of strands needed for the fabric count (two strands for 14-count Aida) and threads them together.
